html:
The land and kingdom of the Dacians, centred on Transylvania, which Rome conquered in 106 CE. The map shows it in 1 BCE and 100 CE.

After King Burebista's realm broke up in 44 BCE, Dacia was a set of smaller states until Decebalus reunited it in the 80s CE. He beat a Roman army sent by the emperor Domitian, then made a peace that left him a paid ally of Rome. Dacia's gold and its threat to the Danube frontier drew Trajan to attack in two wars, in 101 to 102 and 105 to 106 CE. The royal centre at Sarmizegetusa Regia fell, and Decebalus killed himself rather than be captured.

The wars are carved in a spiral story on Trajan's Column in Rome. Dacia became a Roman province, filled with settlers and gold miners, until the emperor Aurelian pulled out around 271 to 275. Modern Romania takes its name and its Latin-based language from this Roman past.
